description:
build_with_aia (pkix-chain/src/lib.rs lines 595-691) loops up to AIA_MAX_DEPTH=5 times. Each iteration:

1. Calls pkix_path_builder::build_first_valid_path — O(pool_size × DFS_BUDGET) in the worst case.
2. Walks the ENTIRE pool to find certs whose issuer is not resolvable (line 634):
       for cert in pool.iter() {
           if issuer_resolvable(cert, &pool, self.anchors) { continue; }
           for uri in aia_extract::ca_issuers_http_uris(cert) { ... }
       }
3. issuer_resolvable itself iterates the pool + anchors for EACH cert (lines 1648-1659):
       pool.iter().any(|c| pkix_path::names_match(...))
           || anchors.iter().any(|a| pkix_path::names_match(...))

Combined cost per iteration of the outer fetch loop: O(pool_size × (pool_size + anchors)) name comparisons, where each names_match is itself O(DN bytes) under RFC 4518 string prep (cheap for short DNs, but not free).

Across iterations the pool only grows: as AIA-fetched certs are added, pool_size goes up. The same orphan checks run on certs that were orphans last round and still are this round.

SCALING IMPACT: For typical PKIs the pool stays small (the caller-supplied chain + ≤5 fetched intermediates). pool_size × (pool_size + anchors) is dominated by O(anchors), which is the trust-store size — 100-200 anchors for a TLS root program. The inner string-prep cost on each anchor adds up: per iteration roughly 5 × 200 × 1µs = 1ms of pure name-comparison overhead, on a hot validation path.

For chains that succeed via the fast path (the common case) this overhead is zero — fast path bypasses build_with_aia entirely. The cost only fires when the chain is incomplete AND AIA fetching is needed, which is the slow path that already involves network I/O. So the per-validation impact is small relative to the I/O.

But verify_batch on incomplete chains pays this cost once per chain. For a batch of 1000 chains needing AIA, that's 1000 × 1ms = 1s of name-comparison overhead amortized across the batch. Not catastrophic but a real cost.

FIX OPTIONS:
- Cache a Set<DN_bytes> of 'resolvable subjects' built once per iteration. Lookups become O(1) (hashmap) instead of O(pool_size + anchors).
- Skip the orphan re-walk for certs that were not orphans last iteration (track a 'definitely-resolvable' set across iterations; only newly-added certs need fresh classification).
- Most importantly: in the common case where AIA succeeds in one round, the second iteration sees no new URIs and exits; this overhead is bounded by 2 × the worst-case cost.

RECOMMENDATION: defer. The cost is bounded by AIA_MAX_DEPTH and dominated by network I/O. Worth revisiting if profiling shows it in a hot path.
title: build_with_aia walks entire pool every iteration to find orphans; O(iterations × pool_size × anchors)
